subject: Commercial alignment: rate equalization, termination liability, and packaging carve-outs
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Amit Shah <amit@neurolytics.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Dec 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Commercial update and sample econ — Redwood proposal v3 attached

Amit — thanks again for the time earlier this week. Per our conversation I attached an updated offer and a simple econ workbook that maps your current run rates to the two packaging options we discussed (Dedicated pool vs Consumption + Reserved burst). High level: we can match your incumbent's effective unit rate on steady-state inference with a 12‑month commitment if you accept a phased onboarding credit and a short pilot to validate throughput.

Ask: can you share the key termination window you need covered (e.g., 90 vs 180 days)? Procurement asked about liability for early decommitment and there’s a path to cap that exposure with a build-down credit.

Attachments: Neurolytics_Econ_Spreadsheet.xlsx (workbook, 120KB); Redwood_Offer_v3.pdf (offer, 48 pages, condensed)

Next steps: if the workbook looks right I’ll route the updated term sheet through Legal and send a DocuSign for signature. If we need to cap decommitment exposure we can include a carve-out in SOW B.

— Mina Haddad
Account Executive, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
min a_haddad@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555‑0192

From: Amit Shah <amit@neurolytics.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procure@neurolytics.ai>
Date: Sat, 11 Dec 2027 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Commercial update and sample econ — Redwood proposal v3 attached

Mina — thanks for the materials. Quick notes after a couple of internal passes: our incumbent (VertexLabs) is offering a three‑month out clause and a pro‑rated credit for any unused reserved capacity; that’s their primary retention lever. Two specific asks from procurement: 1) termination liability cap — we want a predictable maximum in case we pull the plug within year one, and 2) packaging parity — we need a clear side‑by‑side that maps features (KV cache behavior, cold start guarantees, and SLA credits) between your Dedicated pool packaging and the incumbent’s dedicated offer.

On pricing: we see your headline unit numbers, but want to understand the effective blended rate once you include the pilot credit, onboarding support line items, and the first‑90‑day usage anomalies. Procurement also flagged that any material decommitment penalty will go into their risk committee and could derail the bid.

Can Marcus or someone on ops/finance produce a one‑page table that shows: incumbent effective blended rate vs Redwood effective blended rate by month for first 6 months (including credits)? Also a short note on what constitutes a termination event (regulatory, force majeure, business decision) — we need clarity.

Regards,
Amit Shah
Head of Platform Integrations
Neurolytics
[External]
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Amit Shah <amit@neurolytics.ai>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Dec 2027 16:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Commercial update and sample econ — Redwood proposal v3 attached

Amit — thanks for the clarity. I put together a concise comparison and a pragmatic mitigation we’ve used with other mid‑market customers. See summary below (I’ll attach the scoping doc as well):

Summary table (high level) — first 6 months effective blended rate per 1M tokens (USD):
- Incumbent (VertexLabs): Month1 $1,120 | Month2 $980 | Month3 $950 | Month4 $940 | Month5 $930 | Month6 $925
- Redwood (consumption + pilot credit): Month1 $760 (pilot credit applied) | Month2 $980 | Month3 $1,020 (onboarding runup) | Month4 $940 | Month5 $935 | Month6 $930
- Redwood (12m reserved + phased credit): Month1 $900 | Month2 $880 | Month3 $860 | Month4 $850 | Month5 $845 | Month6 $840

Notes: the consumption path shows a favorable Month1 because of the pilot credit but can spike in Month3 during integration testing; the reserved path smooths to a lower long‑term blended rate.

Termination liability options (proposed):
1) Standard decommitment schedule (pro‑rated runout through month 6) — default in the term sheet.
2) Capped liability addendum — we can add an optional addendum that limits Redwood’s termination recoupment to a fixed dollar cap (suggested: $150k for this band) in exchange for a slightly higher committed discount (0.5% on list).
3) Escrowed onboarding credit — we can hold a portion of the onboarding credit in escrow to be released on a validated go‑live to reduce perceived risk.

What constitutes termination: business decision to stop (customer‑initiated), insolvency events, or mutual termination for material breach. Regulatory forced outages or government orders are treated as force majeure and excluded from recoupment. We can tighten language around these buckets in the addendum.

Attachment: termination_liability_scoping.docx (outline of caps and typical language we track in addenda).

If you want, we’ll draft the precise table as a clean PDF for procurement and include the incumbent column with the extracts you shared. Happy to take a quick call Monday to run procurement through the math.

— Marcus Lin
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Dec 2027 15:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Commercial update and sample econ — Redwood proposal v3 attached

Amit — appreciate the diligence. Per Marcus’s analysis and our internal review, here’s a succinct commercial path we can put in an updated SOW that should satisfy procurement and minimize committee friction:

1) Economics: Redwood will offer the 12‑month reserved package at the committed tier in Redwood_Offer_v3.pdf. We will apply a phased onboarding credit equivalent to $75k distributed across the first two months (Month1: $50k, Month2: $25k) to reduce net Month1 exposure.

2) Decommitment cap addendum: optional; cap set at $150k (as Marcus proposed) if you sign the 12‑month reserved. If you prefer the consumption route, we’ll provide Month1 pilot credit ($75k) but no decommitment cap (consumption has natural elasticity).

3) Termination definition: we will adopt mutual language — customer‑initiated business decision triggers pro‑rated runout through month 6; insolvency is treated as termination for cause; force majeure/regulatory events are excluded. We’ll provide the short redline for procurement to review.

4) SLA & packaging parity: we will produce a 1‑page feature parity PDF (KV cache behavior, cold start window, SLA credit schedule) and a side‑by‑side table that you can append to the bid package.

Next step: I’ll drop the addendum + the one‑page parity table into DocuSign and Mina will send the HubSpot deal update. If procurement is comfortable with the $150k cap as presented, we can lock and route for Legal/DocuSign today.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/en/documents/NN-8462-Redwood-Neurolytics
